paragraphs: I'm applying for the Graduate Engineer role in your civil and structural team, advertised on SEEK. The ad welcomes graduates with up to two years' experience and describes estimating, tender documentation and document control work, and that is the side of engineering my study prepared me for.

In February 2026 I completed an Advanced Diploma of Civil Construction Design at Albright Institute. The coursework included cost estimates and bills of quantities, options analysis and risk registers, and reviewing and preparing technical drawings in AutoCAD and Civil 3D to Australian Standards for road, earthworks, pavement and stormwater designs. Reading a drawing set and putting quantities and costs against it is work I have done in study. Before the diploma I completed a Bachelor of Science in Civil Engineering in the Philippines in 2019, which covered structural principles and construction methods.

My site experience is from the Philippines, April 2019 to February 2020, as project-in-charge on a community hall renovation and then field engineer on subdivision finishing works. I reviewed structural and architectural drawings and checked the work against them, tracked procurement and materials, kept material records, site reports and progress reports, and coordinated with engineers, suppliers and subcontractors to sort out site issues. Keeping the records straight so the right drawing was on site is the closest I have come to document control.

Where I fall short of the ad: I have no façade experience and no work experience in Australia yet, I have not used Aconex or Procore, and my degree is from 2019 rather than this year, though my Australian qualification is. I use Excel and Word. I hold a White Card, an Australian driver's licence with my own transport, and full working rights until December 2027 on a Subclass 485 visa. I'm based in Melton, Victoria and open to discussing relocation to Sydney.
My resume is attached and my drawings are at https://macdarenz-droid.github.io/Portfolio. I'd welcome a conversation about the estimating team and what a graduate's first months would look like.

checklist: Decide first whether you would move to Sydney: the letter and email say "open to discussing relocation to Sydney". If the answer is no, do not apply.
The ad asks for Professional Engineer in Training status or willingness to pursue it. The letter says nothing about it; decide your real answer before applying and be ready to say it if asked.
Attach the two PDFs from this record (resume and cover letter).
Paste the screening answers above and fill the notice placeholder.
Press Applied on the tracker with the date and "SEEK".
